Approach step 3 and the rollback plan have the deploy job run the migrate CLI's down step against the production database whenever the post-deploy health check fails. The down file drops the labels column, so every label written between deploy and back-out is destroyed. The back-out is also unnecessary for the stated goal. The column is nullable and additive, so the previous image runs fine against the new schema, and redeploying that image already backs the release out. An automatic, unattended destructive production DDL also acts on a possibly false-positive health check, and a failed or partial down step could leave the schema and image mismatched. Resolve by dropping the automatic down-migration and backing out only by redeploying the previous image. If a schema rollback is wanted, make it an explicit, operator-triggered, audited action with a stated data-loss assumption and the ordering of image redeploy versus schema change.

Criterion ac-release-backed-out ('backed out without operator action') can only be decided against a live production deploy and health check. It carries no requires_live_validation marker, no skip_expected, and no verify_hint. The planned script test only simulates a failing check and cannot show the criterion holds. 'Backed out' is also undefined: it could mean the image only, or the schema as well. Mark the criterion as a declared live walk with an executable verify_hint, or restate it as an observable outcome a sandbox test can decide.

Step 3 and the rollback plan run the migrate CLI's down step against the production database whenever the post-deploy health check fails. For 0104 that drops the labels column and destroys every label written since the release went live. The column is nullable and purely additive, so the previous image runs correctly with it present, and the schema back-out adds data loss without enabling the redeploy. The order is also wrong: the down step runs before the previous image is redeployed, so the new image keeps serving against a schema that no longer matches it. A failed health check can also come from something unrelated to the migration, and the plan has no guard against that. The fix is to make the automatic back-out redeploy the previous image only and leave the additive migration in place. Any schema down-migration in production should be an explicit, gated operator action.
